title: Eﬀect of Soil Composition on Metabolites of Mulberry (Morus sp.) Leaves at Diﬀerent Growth Stages
content: The present study examined the relationships between soil properties and the biochemical composition of mulberry (Morus spp.) leaves at different growth stages in six gardens of Jorhat district, Assam, India. Surface and sub-surface soils were analyzed for pH, organic carbon and available nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. Young, medium-mature and mature leaves were analyzed for total sugar, polyphenols, bound protein, free amino acids, soluble solids and crude fiber. Descriptive statistics, correlation heat-map and partial least squares regression were used to examine the data. Soil reaction was acidic, with mean pH values of 5.07 and 5.05 in the surface and sub-surface layers, respectively. Organic carbon was in medium range for both surface (0.54-0.78% with mean 0.67%) and sub-surface layer (0.51-0.69 with mean 0.61). available nutrients were also in medium range of availability. Mean total sugar content decreased from 10.82 g/kg in young leaves to 9.47 g/kg in medium-mature leaves and 2.80 g/kg in mature leaves. Free amino acid, crud fiber and total soluble solid contents decreased with leaf maturity, whereas, bound protein was found to be in decreasing trend from young leaves (mean content 2.08 g/kg) to medium matured leaves (mean content 1.65 g/kg), then increased slightly at maturity (mean content 1.77 g/kg). Total sugar in young leaves was positively correlated with available phosphorus and potassium at both soil depths. Organic carbon had the largest PLSR coefficients for most biochemical constituents, although the direction of the associations varied with leaf stage and soil depth. The results describe associations between soil properties and leaf biochemical composition within the sampled gardens rather than causal effects.
